summary: Backend testing for the Offers subsystem, hardened auction bidding (atomic CAS + scheduled + proxy + watchers + winner payment), order fulfillment (ship/mark-delivered/payout release), full commissions flow, notification enrichment and payment idempotency. 13/13 pytest tests passed against the deployed preview URL. All Stripe checkout endpoints (offer, auction win, commission deposit, commission balance) return real test-mode checkout_url + session_id. Concurrent-bid race guard confirmed: exactly one of two threaded bids succeeds (409/400 for loser). _apply_paid confirmed idempotent — second invocation on same session_id does not double-create the order. One correctness bug found in proxy-bid pricing (see below).

minor.issue: Proxy vs. proxy ping-pong prices under-market. When two users set competing proxy ceilings (e.g. buyer max=500 vs buyer2 max=300 on start_price=100), _process_proxies alternates by +1 per iteration and hits the internal 30-iter safety cap. Final current_bid ends around ~31 even though the higher proxy should immediately jump to loser_max+1 = 301. Leader identity is correct (higher proxy wins), but the final price is dramatically wrong. Fix: when contender's max exceeds all other proxies, immediately set price to (second_highest_proxy_max + 1) instead of +1 stepping.

Cosmetic: on artist counter/decline/accept, notification kind is `offer_accept`/`offer_counter`/`offer_decline` (from f"offer_{req.action}"). Downstream consumers must match these exact strings; consider standardising to `offer_countered`/`offer_declined`/`offer_accepted` to match the offer status names used elsewhere. Not a bug — flagging inconsistency.

Only allows transition from `pending` — no explicit support for correcting a wrongly-shipped state, no re-ship if buyer disputes. Also no validation that tracking string looks tracking-shaped (any 1–200 char string is accepted).

Race condition: if two accepted offers exist on same artwork (possible if seller accepts multiple offers before any pays), whichever pays first wins and other offers are auto-expired via _apply_paid. But between accept and pay, no lock — buyer B could accept-counter and pay while buyer A is on the Stripe page. Second /pay attempt correctly rejects with `Artwork no longer available` because status flips to `sold` in _apply_paid. Working as designed but worth documenting.

action_items: HIGH: Fix _process_proxies pricing — when higher proxy outbids lower, jump immediately to second-highest ceiling + 1 rather than +1 stepping. Current implementation lets a proxy war on a $500-max vs $300-max end at ~$31 (30-iter cap) instead of ~$301.
OPTIONAL: Rename offer_respond notification kinds to past-tense (`offer_accepted`, `offer_countered`, `offer_declined`) for consistency with offer.status strings.
OPTIONAL: Add regex/length validation on shipping tracking numbers.
OPTIONAL: Add explicit `already_shipped` / `already_paid` error codes to help frontend distinguish 400 states.
critical_code_review_comments: auctions.py _process_proxies (line ~86): 30-iteration cap combined with +1 step means proxy bidding functionally broken for any ceiling delta > 30. Compute second_highest ceiling once and jump directly. Test proves this bug.

auctions.py _enrich (line ~209): calls _finalize inside a GET handler — any read on an expired auction triggers a write. Under bot/preview load this creates lock contention. Move finalize to background task or scheduled job.

offers.py _enrich: does 3 separate awaits per offer (artwork, buyer, artist); listing 200 offers = 600 sequential Mongo round-trips. Batch via $in on user_ids and single artwork lookup, or add caching.
orders.py my_orders / selling_orders: same N+1 pattern — one artwork + one user lookup per line item. For a heavy seller this scales poorly.

payments.py _apply_paid buyer_order branch (line ~366): if tx.items contains the SAME artwork twice, artwork is marked sold once but order records two line items — inventory tracking assumes unit sales but no guard against overselling a single-edition piece. Verify by-design.

auctions.py atomic CAS uses `current_bid: a['current_bid']` in match filter — good — but does NOT re-verify status is still 'live' or end_at hasn't passed. A bid placed exactly at auction end can slip through if _finalize is racing. Consider adding `end_at: {$gt: now}` to the match filter.

offers.py: no explicit expiry sweep — pending offers stay pending forever. Consider a TTL or background job flipping abandoned offers to `expired` after N days. Currently only offers on the same artwork as a paid one get auto-expired.

payments.py pay_offer / pay_auction / etc: five near-identical Stripe session creators. Extract a common helper _create_stripe_session(kind, line_items, metadata, ...) — will cut ~200 lines and reduce drift risk.
payments._apply_paid: no logging on side-effect completion — hard to audit which webhooks ran. Add structured logs (session_id, kind, order_id).
orders.py ship: no idempotency key — retrying a shipped webhook could cause spurious notifications. Guard on fulfillment.status transition (already partially done via 400).

HIGH-PRIORITY BUG for main agent: _process_proxies pricing is broken (bids peak at ~31 in a 100→300 vs 500 proxy war instead of ~301). Leader identity is correct but price is wrong.
rca_of_the_issue: Proxy-bid ping-pong: _process_proxies (auctions.py L83-131) iterates up to 30 times, each iteration bidding target=min(contender.max, current+1). With two active proxies whose ceilings straddle a wide range, the two users alternate as `contender` (since contender must be != current_bidder), and each hop only raises price by +1. After 30 iterations the safety cap trips and the loop returns leaving current_bid at start_price + ~30. Reproduction: create auction start=100 with buyer proxy max=500, then buyer2 proxy max=300 — observed final current_bid=31 with buyer as leader (test_proxy_bid_auto_outbids). Mitigation: before the loop, compute second_highest_active_ceiling = max ceiling among proxies excluding the top one; if the top proxy is not the current leader, set target = min(top.max, second_highest_ceiling + 1) in ONE atomic update instead of stepping.
